verdict.line: You lose if you facetank Boomerang Throw poke before level 6 and get caught scaling into a Mega Gnar all-in; you win if you survive to Trinity Force and turn it into a straight duel.

brief.thesis: Gnar vs Jax win rate sits at 47.6% over 166 games with lane advantage to Gnar but an even solo-kill rate, meaning the deficit is a poke-phase problem, not a dueling one. Gnar is ranged and safe until his Rage bar maxes and forces a transform into Mega Gnar; everything before that point is Gnar poking with Boomerang Throw from range Jax can't answer without E (Counter Strike) or a leap. Once Jax has Trinity Force and R (Relentless Assault) online, the extended-fight math flips back in his favor.

theirWindow.what: OP.GG itself flags this: at max Rage his next ability transforms him into Mega Gnar and he will try to close the gap immediately. Have E (Counter Strike) or Flash ready the moment that bar tops out, don't be mid-animation on a long trade.

yourWindow.when: his Q is thrown and not caught
yourWindow.what: Boomerang Throw returns to him for a cooldown refund if he catches it; if he doesn't, Q is down for its full 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. That's your Leap Strike (Q) window to close and Empower (W) a trade before he has an answer.

start.why: 51.9% win rate over 104 games, the higher-sample start. You're taking repeated Boomerang Throw chip damage as a melee laner against a ranged threat, and the flat damage reduction on autos plus regen offsets exactly that poke.

boots.why: 71.5% pick rate and the larger sample (133 games at 48.9%). Mercury's Treads shows a better rate (57.7%) but on only 26 games — treat Steelcaps as the default and switch to Treads if their CC chain off a Mega Gnar transform is the bigger problem.

core.why: The first item in both measured build paths. It's what turns your Empower (W) procs and R attack speed stacking into real sustained damage once lane stabilizes.
Second item in both listed paths — the on-hit proc and healing let you win the extended trades your R rewards, right as Gnar's early poke advantage expires.
The higher-sample third-item path (14.3% pick over 11 games) after Trinity Force into Sundered Sky — buys you out of a Mega Gnar R stun-into-wall combo once he's transformed.

situational.when: you're taking constant poke damage through the laning phase and need the damage-over-time conversion to survive to your power spike
they're building health to tank your Empower procs or kiting with Hyper move speed
you want earlier kill pressure and a slow to shut down his Hop (E) escape instead of waiting on Trinity's scaling

runes.keystoneWhy: The highest pick rate page (19.4%) and best measured win rate (47.4%). It directly supports the plan of winning once R (Relentless Assault) is up by stacking attack speed on top of attack speed for longer fights, which is exactly where Jax's curve turns in his favor.

summoners.why: 52.5% win rate and 60.2% pick rate, the clear default. Gnar's poke-heavy pattern keeps him at partial health often; Ignite converts that chip damage into kill pressure before his level-6 Mega Gnar power spike arrives.

playing.title: Time Counter Strike on his autos
playing.detail: E (Counter Strike) dodges all incoming basic attacks, so use it right as Gnar swings to deny his auto-reset harass and the stun lands on him when he's in range to be punished.

playing.title: Trade only when his Q is dead
playing.detail: If Boomerang Throw misses or isn't caught on return, it's down for its full cooldown. That's your window to Leap Strike (Q) in and Empower (W) a trade before he can poke you again.

playing.title: Respect a full Fury bar
playing.detail: At max Rage his next ability transforms him and he closes distance immediately. Don't be committed to a long trade when that bar tops out — have E or Flash free.

playing.title: Keep trades short before level 6
playing.detail: Lane favors Gnar through this stretch (47.6% head-to-head). Poke back when you land Empower, then disengage rather than standing in his auto range.

playing.title: Commit once R is up
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has 0 cooldown and every third consecutive attack hits harder — extended fights reward you more than short pokes once you have it.

playing.title: Don't walk into Mega Gnar's W
playing.detail: Transformed, his W becomes Wallop, a frontal stun, not the Hyper speed buff. Bait it with your Leap Strike positioning instead of approaching head-on.

playing.title: Save Ignite for the mid-health window
playing.detail: His own poke keeps him at partial health often — Ignite plus an Empowered auto closes kills before he can disengage with Hop (E).

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, item paths, runes and summoner splits above are measured from real games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning tying them together — the trade windows, the Fury-bar read, the power-curve timing — is this brief's own analysis, not OP.GG's.
